extracted.intended_audience: independent filmmakers, theatre artists, composers, and general readers interested in the Sundance Institute and its programs
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize the Sundance Institute's programs, labs, fellowships, and institutional activities that support independent filmmakers, theatre artists, composers, and related practitioners. The page describes program goals, formats, selection notes, and operational constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature Film Program — Directors Lab format and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: For three weeks each June in Sundance, Directors Lab Fellows rehearse, shoot and edit four to six scenes from their screenplays under the mentorship of accomplished directors, editors, cinematographers and actors who serve as Creative Advisors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to creative support through Labs and workshops, the Institute helps independent filmmakers complete their work through various grants and fellowships, many of which are designated for filmmakers selected to participate in the Feature Film Program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Film Music Program / Composers Lab objective
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sundance Institute Composers Lab, held every summer at Skywalker Sound, aims to enhance the role of music in independent film.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program offers mentorship and advisors (listed alumni and advisors), and the Music Cafe provides performance and daytime programming during the Sundance Film Festival. Composers Lab alumni and advisor networks are part of the program's support structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Native American and Indigenous Film Program — participation & outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilitates the participation of Native and Indigenous artists in the Institute's artistic development programs and the Sundance Film Festival, and expanded in 2008 to include outreach to documentarians, theatre artists, and musicians seeking support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program activities include enabling festival participation, hosting the annual Native Forum (panel discussions, workshops, networking), and providing pathways to the Documentary Fund, Theatre Program, and Film Music Program. Supported by named foundations and partners; historically had dedicated screening category (1994–2004) and incorporated Native films into official program since 2005.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theatre Program — development process & constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports development of independent theatre via Theatre Labs where projects rehearse every other day to allow playwrights time for rewrites; projects are assigned a Sundance dramaturg and collaborate with the Producing Artistic Director prior to residency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no physically controllable space (e.g., 'black box'); lighting and scenic production values are not available, though designers may sometimes participate. The Playwright's Retreat at Ucross is an 18-day writing colony (five playwrights + composer) for early-stage development. Artists are selected by invitation only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentary Film Program — support & grant cadence
rubrics_metrics.description: Assists nonfiction filmmakers with workshops in editing, storytelling, and scoring, and provides grants to nonfiction film projects through the Sundance Documentary Fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program encourages exploration of innovative nonfiction storytelling, promotes exhibition to broader audiences, and supports artists year-round via labs, the Documentary Composers Laboratory, Edit and Story Laboratory, festival panels, and international initiatives. Documentary Fund grants are announced once a year.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Frontier — innovation & boundary-pushing focus
rubrics_metrics.description: New Frontier Labs and residency programs foster works of boundary-pushing artists and technologists, marked by central themes of innovation and unconventionalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The New Frontier exhibition curates projects that may combine fiction, non-fiction, transmedia storytelling, multimedia installations, performances, virtual reality segments, and immersive installations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative Producing Initiative — producer-centered training
rubrics_metrics.description: A 5-day Creative Producing Lab focusing on the producer as a whole, giving fellows the chance to explore cinematic material and develop skills needed in scripting and editing stages with experienced advisors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes fellowships and mentorship from experienced producers; the initiative supports next-generation independent producers and has produced fellows whose feature works are named as examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episodic Storytelling Initiative — writers' development for serial content
rubrics_metrics.description: Year-round program of Episodic Story Labs for 10 writers (or co-writing teams) to work with accomplished showrunners, non-writing creative producers, and studio and network executives to refine episodic-writing/producing skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiated in response to growth in serialized content for online and television platforms; addresses the unique needs of serialized work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sundance Ignite — youth short film challenge structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Short film challenge for young filmmakers ages 18 to 24 partnered with Adobe's Project 1324; entrants can win the Ignite Ticket Package and the Ignite Fellows Program (year-round festival and industry experience).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also includes Ignite On Tour for winners to engage with Institute staff and alumni; supported by named academic and corporate partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative Distribution Initiative (CDI) — distribution & marketing guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Part of the Creative Producing Initiative; CDI provides online resources, workshops, and a network of organizations to teach distribution and marketing of independent film.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Sundance alumni, CDI offers free consultations on Kickstarter campaigns and other distribution strategies; cited example: first release under CDI was the 2017 film Columbus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sundance Collection at UCLA — preservation & archival mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintains a collection at UCLA to conserve and archive the history of independent film, addressing the pressing need for film preservation due to chemical decomposition, neglect, and changing ownership of film libraries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Collection holds over 300 film prints and related materials (press kits, interviews) to create a living record of independent film history and provide a resource for study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection & participation notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Various programs and labs have selection or participation policies (e.g., 'Artists are selected by invitation only' for certain Theatre programs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants and fellowships are often designated for participants in specific Institute programs; some programmatic details include annual grant cycles (Documentary Fund) or limited cohort sizes (Episodic Labs for 10 writers).
